proposed_widenings.name: create_object.conditional_size_by_material
proposed_widenings.justification: The spell imposes a smaller maxSize (medium) for metal/stone/mineral materials vs. large for everything else. create_object has only one maxSize field with no material-conditional branching. Two separate direct phases can't express a material-conditional choice because there's no phase-level predicate on the attached object's material.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If you're working with metal, stone, or another mineral substance, however, the fabricated object can be no larger than Medium (contained within a 5-foot Cube).

proposed_widenings.name: ObjectMaterial.stone_or_mineral
proposed_widenings.justification: ObjectFilter.material only covers 'metal' and 'flammable'. Fabricate's size restriction applies to stone and other minerals, which has no matching ObjectMaterial variant.
proposed_widenings.evidence: If you're working with metal, stone, or another mineral substance...

proposed_widenings.name: create_object.proficiency_gate
proposed_widenings.justification: The spell forbids creating high-skill items (weapons, armor) unless the caster has proficiency with the relevant Artisan's Tools. No predicate gate on create_object can express a caster-proficiency check.
proposed_widenings.evidence: You also can't use it to create items that require a high degree of skill—such as weapons and armor—unless you have proficiency with the type of Artisan's Tools used to craft such objects.

notes: Core mechanic (instantaneous object creation from raw materials via activation/direct/create_object) encodes cleanly. Typecheck passes; tracer emits a valid graph. Three omitted riders: (1) material-conditional size cap (large → medium for minerals), (2) missing 'stone_or_mineral' ObjectMaterial variant, (3) Artisan's Tools proficiency gate on certain fabrications. All three are surface_widening gaps — the v4 taxonomy has create_object; what's missing is a conditional/predicate layer on the atom and a wider ObjectMaterial enum.
